answer: Sybil resistance means making identity cheap to hold but expensive to use. Under this scheme a newcomer must forge a sponsorship chain: three established members each post a slashable bond and publicly sign the new key, so a thousand fake accounts need three thousand real backers. Reputation then accumulates like a glacier, one verified job per layer, and it thaws when a sponsor goes dormant. Honest newcomers get a sandbox haven with escrowed payouts until their melt depth clears a threshold; farms stall there, burning weeks per key.
